title: Sets and Venn Diagrams: Grouping Things Precisely

questions.question: If A = {2, 4, 6, 8}, which statement is true?
questions.rationale: 4 is an element of A, written 4 ∈ A. Note that {4} is a set containing 4 — a subset of A, not an element of it.

questions.question: How many subsets does a set with 4 elements have?
questions.rationale: Each element is either in or out of a subset — a binary choice — so the count is 2^4 = 16. The formula n(P(A)) = 2^n covers every size from empty to full.

questions.question: How many PROPER subsets does {a, b, c} have?
questions.rationale: A 3-element set has 2^3 = 8 subsets; a proper subset excludes the set itself, leaving 8 − 1 = 7.

questions.question: With A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}, what is A − B?
questions.rationale: The difference A − B keeps elements of A that are not in B: strip away the shared 3 and 4 to leave {1, 2}.

questions.question: With U = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} and A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, what is A'?
questions.rationale: The complement holds everything in the universe that is missing from A: 5 and 6. Complements always depend on the chosen U.

questions.question: By De Morgan's laws, (A ∪ B)' equals:
questions.rationale: The complement of a union is the intersection of the complements: 'not (A or B)' means 'not A and not B'. The twin law swaps the roles: (A ∩ B)' = A' ∪ B'.

questions.question: In a class of 40, 25 take mathematics, 20 take physics, and 8 take both. How many take at least one subject?
questions.rationale: Inclusion–exclusion: n(M ∪ P) = 25 + 20 − 8 = 37. Adding without subtracting the 8 shared students double-counts them.

questions.question: In that same class, how many students take neither subject?
questions.rationale: The union covered 37 of the 40 students, so 40 − 37 = 3 sit outside both circles — the Venn rectangle's leftover region.

questions.question: Of 100 students: 45 play cricket, 38 football, 30 hockey; 12 play cricket and football, 10 cricket and hockey, 8 football and hockey; 4 play all three. How many play at least one sport?
questions.rationale: Three-set inclusion–exclusion: 45 + 38 + 30 − 12 − 10 − 8 + 4 = 87. Pairwise overlaps are subtracted, but the triple overlap — subtracted three times — must be added back once.

questions.question: In that survey, how many students play at least two sports?
questions.rationale: 'Exactly two' counts (12−4) + (10−4) + (8−4) = 18, but 'at least two' pulls the all-three centre back in: 18 + 4 = 22.
